chapter_theme: The most subtle five letters: chanting சிவாய and சிவசிவ with a fixed mind brings bliss and a heart the Lord never leaves; the one letter of the Lord outweighs all Vedic and Agamic learning, and those who boast of knowing letters do not know the letter that masters them.
structure_note: Two verses on practice, the mind fixed by the mantra (2718) and the yogic ascent through the five (2719), then two on the one letter against book learning (2720, 2721).

2718.reading: Fixing the mind with சிவாய நம and making oneself wholly a servant so that harm is gone, then thinking சிவாய சிவசிவ again and again, the mind stands with its harm destroyed, and that is bliss.
2718.nuance: The verse moves from the full mantra (சிவாய நம) to its subtle forms (சிவாய, சிவசிவ). அவாயம் is apaya, harm or danger, and also echoes அவா, desire, so 'harm' may be the craving that troubles the mind.

2719.reading: Passing through the orb of red flame and beyond it, climbing by the five in their order and taking the way, at the time he spoke of one may attain the state in which the Lord never leaves, as one's own heart.
2719.nuance: செஞ்சுடர் மண்டலம் (the orb of red flame) is traditionally a centre in the yogic body, the sun's or fire's region; அஞ்சு அணவும் முறை may be the five letters placed in order along the body or the five states. துஞ்சும் அவன் சொன்ன காலத்து is obscure: துஞ்சு can mean sleep or death, so it may be the time of death the Lord appointed or the yogic sleep.

2720.reading: Though one recites the Vedas with their limbs and the Agamas, what is ours lies in one letter of our Lord; master that one letter with doubt destroyed and one becomes a precious vessel that has reached the farther shore.
2720.nuance: அங்கம் are the six limbs of the Veda. The one letter is not named; tradition takes it as சி or as the five letters held as one, or as Om. அருங்கலம் can be a rare ship or a rare jewel; with அங்கரை (that shore) the ship fits better, with the shore as the end of births.

2721.reading: The five that ripened lie within the ancient Veda; none know the karma that wakes there and sleeps; fools say 'we know the letters', but they do not know the letter that masters the letters.
2721.nuance: பழுத்தன ஐந்தும் பழமறையுள்ளே is traditionally taken as the five letters set at the centre of the Veda (in the Sri Rudram of the Yajur Veda). Line 2 is obscure: விழித்து அங்கு உறங்கும் வினை may be karma that seems to sleep but wakes. எழுத்தை அழுத்தும் எழுத்து (the letter that presses down the letters) plays on letters as script and as mantra.

links.note: Both answer endless learning with a choice: the Naladiyar says learning has no shore and life is short, so take only what is fitting, as the swan takes milk from water; Tirumular names the one thing to take, the Lord's letter, and makes it the vessel that does reach the shore.

Both picture release as crossing to a shore: the Kural's great sea of births is crossed only by those who reach the Lord's feet, and in 2720 the one who masters the Lord's letter is a vessel that has reached the farther shore.

The Kural calls letters and numbers the two eyes of the living; 2721 calls those who boast of knowing letters fools, because they don't know the letter that masters letters. The difference rests on எழுத்து meaning script in the Kural and the mantra in Tirumular, so it qualifies rather than contradicts.

940 says the Vedic man esteemed by birth is not the true one; the மறையவன் in whom the five letters stand becomes those letters. 2721 says the five lie ripened within the ancient Veda (பழமறை யுள்ளே), and those who boast 'we know the letters' (எழுத்துஅறிவோம்) do not know the letter that masters letters. Both set the five letters above learning of the Veda as such.
